extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / scientists and readers of scientific method (early modern and scholarly audiences)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and methodological standards for reconstructing natural philosophy using Bacon's Novum Organum: how to collect natural history, design experiments, purge intellectual idols, and employ a new form of induction to discover causes and build useful sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and openness of presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Omnia, quantum fieri potest, aperte et perspicue proponantur (all things should be proposed openly and clearly). Nuditas animi ... innocentiae et simplicitatis comes est.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the order and content plainly; avoid premature abstractive reasoning that hides the thing; include clear descriptions, examples, and where a notion is obscure add examples or an already-made part to illustrate the whole. The work's parts should be explicit and transparent to aid understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer induction over syllogistic demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: We reject syllogism for explaining nature and employ induction: 'Inductionem enim censemus eam esse demonstrandi formam... quae sensum tuetur et naturam premit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on syllogistic chains from verbal propositions; instead derive principles from properly-constructed inductions rooted in experience. Avoid treating dialectical victory as a substitute for operative knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of discovery: particular-to-general via controlled induction
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordo quoque demonstrandi invertitur ... axiomata continenter et gradatim excitantur, ut nonnisi postremo loco ad generalissima veniatur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ascend gradually from well-examined particulars to carefully formed axioms; do not leap to generalities from weak or vague notions. Ensure general propositions are well-terminated and adhere to nature's reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induction must be eliminative and decisive (not mere enumeration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inductionem ... quae experientiam solvat et separet, et per exclusiones ac rejectiones debitas necessario concludat; simple enumeration is puerile and precarious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exclusions, rejections, and structured eliminative procedures to arrive at causes; avoid simple lists of instances that risk contradiction by counter-instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use instruments and artful experiments to supplement and correct the senses
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimentorum longe major est subtilitas quam sensus ipsius, licet instrumentis exquisitis adjuti ... experimentum de re judicet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on designed experiments and instruments as substitutes or correctives for fallible sense perception. Design experiments 'perite et secundum artem' to probe nature beyond naked senses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design experiments for subtle and sometimes non‑obvious phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Conquirimus genus experimentorum longe subtilius et simplicius ... complura a tenebris educimus et erui-mus, quae nulli in mentem venisset investigare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include experiments that reveal inconspicuous facts (even if they seem useless alone) because they form the alphabet of later discoveries. Aim for subtle, carefully contrived trials rather than only obvious tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct a curated natural history oriented to discovering causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Proponimus historiam naturalem, quae ... lucem inventioni causarum affundat, et philosophiae enutricandae primam mammam praebeat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect observations and histories not for mere variety or spectacle, but to furnish material that illuminates causes and feeds the active part of science. Prefer data that aid invention of axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and vet observations strictly; exclude fables and fraudulent reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Nihil referatur auctum miraculi causa, sed quae narramus a fabulis et vanitate casta et intemerata sint ... recepta quaeque ac jactata mendacia nominatim proscribimus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept only faithfully seen or well-attested observations; proscribe received myths, superstitions, and longstanding falsehoods from the corpus of natural history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report experimental method and procedures transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: In omni experimento novo ... modum tamen experimenti quo usi sumus aperte subjungimus; ut ... videant homines quid erroris subesse et adhaerere possit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an explicit account of how experiments were carried out so others can assess potential errors and reproduce or refine the tests; add cautions, scruples and notes to expose the reliability limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and correct for sensory error; use auxiliaries to sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensus enim fallunt ... ut his occurratur, nos multo et fido ministerio auxilia sensui undique conquisivimus et contraximus, ut destitutionibus substitutiones, variationibus rectificationes suppeditentur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize both absence and deception of senses; provide substitutions, variations and rectifications (instruments, repeated experiments) to counter these faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and purge 'idola' (prejudices) obstructing inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Idola ... ad quibus occupatur mens, vel Adscititia sunt vel Innata ... haec nullo modo evelli possunt; id tantum relinquitur ut indicentur atque ut vis ista mentis insidiatrix notetur et convincatur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark and bring to light the idols (ingrained errors) of the mind—both acquired and innate—so they can be exposed and neutralized; use structured induction to prevent old errors from reappearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fortify the foundations of the sciences and test received principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamenta quoque scientiarum fortius deprimimus et solidamus, atque initia inquirendi alius sumimus ... illia ipsa principia putativa ad rationes reddendas compellere quousque plane constent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject putative first principles to scrutiny; compel accepted notions to be justified by new judgments and evidences rather than assumed from tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide exemplars and typologies as models of discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Exempla proponantur inquirendi ... typos et plasmata, quae universum mentis processum atque inveniendi continuatam fabricam et ordinem ... in certis subjectis ... sub oculos ponant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give worked examples in diverse and noble subjects to illustrate the method and provide templates people can follow; these are applied particulars of the method for learning and imitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep provisional parts and allow suspension of judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Quinta pars ad tempus tantum ... adhibetur ... usque dum sors haberi possit ... istam vero judicii suspensionem non est quod exhorreat quispiam ... donee mens in causarum explicatione consistat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow a provisional collection of inventions/observations to be held in suspension until they are verified by the full method; do not force premature final judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for operative arts and inventions, not merely verbal disputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Huic nostrae scientiae finis proponitur, ut inveniantur non argumenta sed artes, ... Itaque ex intentione diversa diversus sequitur effectus. Illic adversarius disputatione vincitur; hic natura opere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on producing usable arts, techniques, and instruments (operative knowledge) rather than winning dialectical arguments; valorize practice and results over rhetorical victory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble histories not only of bodies but of primary 'virtues' or properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Neque Corporum tantum historiam exhibemus; sed ... Virtutum ipsarum ... historiam seorsum comparare (Denso, Raro, Calido, Frigido, Consistenti, Fluido...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record systematic histories of primary qualities (density, heat, cold, consistency, etc.) as separate investigations to support causal inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overreliance on dialectic and professorial authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialetica ... ad errores potius figendos quam ad veritatem aperiendam valuit ... nulla spes majoris augmenti sita est nisi in restauratione quadam scientiarum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let scholastic disputation or appeal to ancient authority supplant methodical experimental inquiry; reward practical augmentation of knowledge over rhetorical skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize the work into complementary parts serving discovery and cultivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Partes operis a nobis constituuntur sex ... duae doctrinarum emanationes ... alia scientias colendi, alia inveniendi ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the enterprise into distinct but allied parts (e.g., partitions of sciences, instruments for interpretation, phenomena, scale of intellect, prodromi, active philosophy) so that cultivation and invention are both served and not conflated.
